title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore West on 1970-02-08

ai_review.summary: A solid composite source captures a stellar early‑70 set with a smoking Smokestack Lightning, epic Lovelight and standout Dark Star, though the mix is a bit tinny and drums sit low.
ai_review.review: The performance is widely praised – opening with a blazing Smokestack Lightning, soaring through a superb Dark Star, a tight St. Stephen > Not Fade Away > St. Stephen sandwich and an expansive Lovelight that many call one of the year’s best. The recording is a mixed‑source composite (soundboard + audience) that sounds better than average but suffers from tinny/phased qualities, low drum levels and occasional balance issues.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers rave about the musical performance (high show quality) while noting consistent but moderate recording flaws; weighted average yields a rating just above 4.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Composite of soundboard and audience sources; generally clearer than average, but drums are low, the mix can be tinny/phased, and balance is off in places.

standout_songs: China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
Sitting on Top of the World
St. Stephen > Not Fade Away > St. Stephen
show_quality.setlist_flow: A thunderous Smokestack opener sets the tone, followed by a classic early‑70 sandwich of St. Stephen/NFA/St. Stephen and an extended Lovelight that closes the show on a high, giving the set a strong, flowing arc.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar is frequently highlighted – perfect tone on Smokestack, chiming leads in China Cat, digging deep during Not Fade Away and driving the long Lovelight jam.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir’s rhythm work and vocal interplay with Garcia are praised, especially in the early set and the St. Stephen sandwich.
band_member_comments.Drums: Multiple reviewers note the drums sit a bit low in the mix; overall drumming is solid but masked by recording balance issues.
